title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Student submits assignment without full awareness of how the Grades Portal will process, store, or share the work file, student id, course, and timestamp for purposes beyond grading.
assumptions: Student may not read privacy policy or understand data retention.

title: Linkability via metadata
description: The data flow links the student's identity (via student id) with the submission content and timestamp, enabling correlation of activities.
assumptions: Flow metadata or content can be observed or logged.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify encryption or anonymization of flow.

title: Disclosure of assignment content
description: Grades Portal receives and potentially stores the work file which may contain personal or sensitive information from the student.
assumptions: Work file could include personal details; portal may have broad access.

title: Identifier in transit
description: The data flow carries student id which is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (student).
assumptions: Student id qualifies as identifying per the knowledge base.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service receives and processes identified data such as student id, course, file reference and requesting role.
uncertainty_note: Applies context from retrieved I.1.1 node.

title: Storage of identifiable assignment data
description: The Assignment Store receives and persists the submitted assignment file along with student id, course, and submission time, constituting a disclosure and storage of personal data that should be minimized per the minimality principle.
assumptions: The assignment file and metadata qualify as personal data under applicable regulations.

title: Processing of identified teacher request data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes the login and queue request which contains identified data about the teacher and their courses, enabling identification of the individual making the request.
assumptions: The request includes authentication details or session data that identifies the teacher.

title: Linkability of teacher to course submissions via request metadata
description: The data flow from teacher to portal may allow linking the teacher's identity (via login) to specific course queues and submissions being reviewed.
assumptions: Network observers or logs can correlate the authenticated request with course data.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly cover linkability tree nodes; based on general LINDDUN applicability for EE->Process flows.

title: Identifiability of students via names in submissions
description: The process shares student names along with their work content and submission times, directly identifying individuals to the recipient.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify if names are necessary or if pseudonyms could be used instead.

title: Disclosure of submission content during display
description: Student work content and associated metadata are sent over the data flow from the web app to the teacher, exposing potentially sensitive personal or academic information.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the flow may traverse networks without additional protection details provided.

title: Teacher unawareness of data handling obligations
description: The external entity (teacher) receives identifiable student data without modeled awareness of privacy responsibilities for storage or further use of submissions.
uncertainty_note: No specific details on teacher training or policies in the flow description.

title: Teacher unawareness of data handling
description: The teacher may lack full awareness regarding how the recorded grade, feedback text, student id and grader id will be further processed, stored, accessed or potentially shared by the Grades Portal, leading to unawareness threats for the student's personal data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive student performance data in transit
description: The data flow transmits identifiable information including student grades and written feedback; without adequate protection this could result in disclosure of confidential educational records.

title: Non-compliance risk in processing educational records
description: The receiving process may fail to handle the student grade and feedback data in compliance with applicable privacy regulations (e.g. FERPA or GDPR) for educational personal data.

title: Identifiability of students via grade records
description: The Grade Records Database receives and stores records containing student id along with course, grade, feedback, grader id and timestamp, directly identifying individual students and their academic performance.

title: Disclosure of sensitive grade and feedback data
description: Storage of detailed grade records including feedback in DS2 creates risk of unauthorized disclosure of personal academic information if the datastore lacks adequate access controls or encryption.

title: Linkability of student identity to grades in transit
description: The data flow DF7 carries student id linked to specific course, grade and feedback, enabling linking of identity to performance data while the record is in transit to the database.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Grades Portal Web App receives and processes the student's request containing identified data (e.g. student ID or authentication token) to fetch and return their grades and feedback.
assumptions: The request flow includes data that identifies the student, which is necessary for the functionality but creates an identifiability threat.

title: Interception of grades and feedback during transmission
description: Grades and teacher feedback constitute personal data; transmission from the portal to the student over the data flow could be intercepted if not properly encrypted, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the web app uses HTTP or unencrypted channel for display
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify transport security; this is a common web-app concern for personal data flows

title: Student unawareness of data processing details
description: The process shares grades/feedback without necessarily informing the student about retention, third-party sharing, or purpose of processing the displayed data.
uncertainty_note: May be covered in privacy policy but flow itself does not guarantee awareness

title: Detectability of student accessing personal grades
description: Receipt of the data at the external entity (student) could allow detection of the student's activity or interests if the client-side receipt is observable (e.g., browser history, network logs on student device).
uncertainty_note: Outside system boundary but per LINDDUN Pro position D applies to recipient

title: Parent unawareness of data linkage implications

title: Parent unawareness of data handling practices

title: Identifiability via account records in transit
description: The data flow transmits account records containing identifiable information and relationship links, making individuals identifiable during the write operation.

title: Explicit transfer of full personal records to third-party cloud

assumptions: Grade records and account data include personal identifiable information.

title: Third-party storage and potential secondary use of sensitive educational data
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider (EE5) receives and stores full personal grade and account data, enabling possible further disclosures or processing beyond the intended backup replication.

assumptions: Views built from full records may involve processing beyond original collection purpose.

title: Non-compliance with student data regulations
